agenda_text:
City Council of Monterey Park
  The City Council Acting on Behalf of the Successor Agency of the Former Redevelopment
 Agency, the Housing Authority, the Monterey Park Financing Authority and the Monterey Park
  Geologic Hazard Abatement District Agenda

  Regular Meeting
  Monterey Park City Hall Council Chambers
  320 West Newmark Avenue, Monterey Park, CA 91754

  Wednesday, July 2, 2025
  6:30 PM
  Mission Statement
The mission of the City of Monterey Park is to provide excellent service, foster growth and opportunity,
  and create a joyous and collaborative environment.
  Land Acknowledgment
We would like to acknowledge that the land we inhabit today was once known as Tovangaar, the home
 of the Gabrieleño-Tongva people. We show our respect to the Gabrieleño-Tongva people, as well as
  all Indigenous people, past, present, and future, and honor their labor as original caretakers of this
land. We commit to uplifting the Gabrieleño-Tongva people, invite you to acknowledge the history, and
  join us in caring for this land.

General Information
Documents related to an Agenda item are available to the public in the City Clerk’s Office located at
320 West Newmark Avenue, Monterey Park, CA 91754, during normal business hours and
at www.montereypark.ca.gov/agendas.

The public may watch the meeting live on the city’s cable channel MPKTV (AT&T U-verse, channel 99
or Charter Communications, channel 182) or by visiting the city’s website
at http://www.montereypark.ca.gov/133/City-Council-Meeting-Videos. Per the Americans with
Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please call City Hall at
(626) 307-1359 for reasonable accommodation at least 24 hours before a meeting. Council Chambers
are wheelchair accessible.

Public Participation
You may speak up to 5 minutes on an/each Agenda item. You may combine up to 2 minutes of time
with another person’s speaking. No person may speak more than a total of 10 minutes. The Mayor
and City Council may change the amount of time allowed for speakers. Written Communication will be
accepted up to 24 hours before the meeting by completing an online form
at www.montereypark.ca.gov/writtencomm.

While all comments are welcome, the Brown Act does not allow the City Council to take action on any
item not on the agenda. The Council may briefly respond to comments after Public Communications is
 closed. Persons may, in addition to any other matter within the City Council's subject-matter
jurisdiction, comment on Agenda Items at this time. If you provide public comment on a specific
Agenda item at this time, however, you cannot later provide comments at the time the Agenda Item is
considered.

1.  Call to Order
  Mayor

2.  Flag Salute
  The Monterey Park Fire Explorers

3.  Roll Call
  Henry Lo, Vinh Ngo, Jose Sanchez, Thomas Wong, Elizabeth Yang

4.  Agenda Additions, Deletions, Changes and Adoptions

5.  Public Communications

6.  Staff Communications

  6.A. Library

  6.B. Recreation and Community Services

  6.C. Public Works

7.  Presentation

  7.A. Development Projects Update

  7.B. Economic Development Strategic Plan Update

8.  Old Business

9.  Consent Calendar
  All items under the Consent Calendar are considered by the City Council to be routine and will be
  enacted by one motion. Specific items may be removed from the Consent Calendar at the request
  of any member of the City Council for separate consideration.

  9.A. Monthly Investment Report

  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Receiving and filing the monthly investment report; and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

  9.B. Resolution approving the Memorandum of Understanding between the City and the
  Monterey Park Police Officers' Association for the term of July 1, 2025 to June 20,
  2028
   It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Adopting a Resolution approving a Memorandum of Understanding ("MOU") between
  the City of Monterey Park and the Monterey Park Police Officers' Association
  ("MPPOA"). The MPPOA represents the police corporals and police officers in the
  Monterey Park Police Department; and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

9.C. Receive and File Housing Element Correspondence with California Department of
  Housing and Community Development

  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Receiving and filing the report; and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

9.D. Maintenance Agreement with Trojan Technologies Corp.

  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Authorizing the City Manager to execute an Agreement with Trojan Technologies
  Corp., (“Trojan”) in a form approved by the City Attorney, for the maintenance of its
  Advanced-Oxidation Ultraviolet Treatment System at a cost not to exceed $315,000;
  and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

  CEQA (California Environmental Quality Act):
  These actions are exempt from additional review under the California Environmental Quality
  Act (California Public Resources Code §§ 2100, et seq., “CEQA”) and CEQA Guidelines (14
  California Code of Regulations §§ 15000, et seq.) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines §
  15061(b)(3), the common sense exemption that CEQA applies only to projects which have
  the potential for causing a significant effect on the environment applies to the recommended
  action. It can be seen with certainty that there is no possibility that the proposed action has a
  significant effect on the environment.

9.E. A Resolution Declaring the Month of July as “Parks Make Life Better” Month in the
  City of Monterey Park

  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Adopting a Resolution declaring the month of July as “Parks Make Life Better” Month
  in the City of Monterey Park; and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

9.F. Consideration to provide Letter of Support for SB 627, the "No Secret Police Act," and
  SB 805, the “No Vigilantes Act," on behalf of the City
   It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. If desirable, sending a letter of support for California Senate Bills 627, the "No Secret
  Police Act," and 805, the “No Vigilantes Act,” on behalf of the City;
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

10. Public Hearing

  10.A. Adoption of an Ordinance Amending Title 6 of the Monterey Park Municipal Code in
  its entirety regarding public health services and incorporation of Title 11 of the Los
  Angeles County Code

  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Opening the continued public hearing; taking testimonial and documentary evidence;
  closing the public hearing;
  2. After considering the evidence, adopting an ordinance amending Title 6 of the
  Monterey Park Municipal Code; and
  3. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

  10.B. Adoption of an Ordinance Updating the Fire Hazard Severity Zones ("FHSZ") Pursuant
  to Government Code section 51178

  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Opening the continued public hearing; taking testimonial and documentary evidence;
  closing the public hearing;
  2. After considering the evidence, adopting an ordinance adopting the finalized State
  Responsibility Area Fire Hazard Severity Zone map; and
  3. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

  CEQA (California Environmental Quality Act):
  The City reviewed the environmental impacts of the extension under the California
  Environmental QualityAct (Public Resources Code §§ 21000, et seq. "CEQA") and the
  regulations promulgated thereunder (14 Cal. Code of Regs. §§ 15000, et. seq., the "CEQA
  Guidelines"). This activity contemplates administrative actions and will not result in any
  direct or indirect physical change in the environment. Accordingly, no further review is
  required.

11. New Business

12. City Communications (City Council) / Future Agenda Items

13. Closed Session (if Required; City Attorney to Announce)

14. Adjourn

  MINUTES
  MONTEREY PARK CITY COUNCIL
  FINANCING AUTHORITY (MPFA)
  HOUSING AUTHORITY (MPHA)
  GEOLOGIC HAZARD ABATEMENT DISTRICT (GHAD)
  SUCCESSOR AGENCY (SA)
  REGULAR MEETING
  JULY 2, 2025

The City Council, the Financing Authority (MPFA), the Housing Authority (MPHA), the
Geologic Hazard Abatement District (GHAD), and the Successor Agency (SA) of the
City of Monterey Park held a Regular Meeting of the Council in the Council Chamber,
located at 320 West Newmark Avenue in the City of Monterey Park, Wednesday, July 2,
2025 at 6:30 p.m.

1.  Call to Order: Mayor Ngo called the meeting to order at 7:13 p.m.

2.  Flag Salute: The Monterey Park Fire Explorers led the flag salute. Pledge of
  Allegiance presented by Civic Superstar Hilde Wilson.

3.  Roll Call:
  Assistant Deputy City Clerk Helena Cho called the roll:

  Council Members Present: Henry Lo, Vinh Ngo, Jose Sanchez, Thomas Wong
  Elizabeth Yang
  Council Members Absent: None.

  Also Present:
  City Treasurer Amy Lee
  City Manager Inez Alvarez
  City Attorney Karl Berger
  Director of Human Resources and Risk Management Christine Tomikawa
  Director of Recreation and Community Services Robert Aguirre
  Acting City Librarian LV Frazier
  Director of Public Works Shawn Igoe
  Police Chief Scott Wiese
  Interim Fire Chief Scott Haberle
  Police Captain Gus Jimenez
  Fire Battalion Chief Ryan Weddle
  IT Manager Martin Dinh
  Economic Development Manager Joeseph Torres
  Planning Manager Beth Chow
  Library Manager Linda Vera
  Recreation and Community Services Manager Christina Alatorre
  Principal Management Analyst Rebecca Bojorquez

  MISSION STATEMENT
 The mission of the City of Monterey Park is to provide excellent service, foster growth and opportunity,
  and create a joyous and collaborative environment.
  .
   73-204
  July 2, 2025
  Recreation and Community Services Program Coordinator Guillermo Chavez
  Recreation and Community Services Program Coordinator Alejandra Espinosa
  Administrative Aide Cristina Garcia
  Office Assistant II Michelle Martinez

  Virtually Present: Director of Finance Martha Garcia

4.  Agenda Additions, Deletions, Changes and Adoptions:
  Mayor Ngo read a statement authorizing City Attorney Berger to take all action
  needed to file a motion to intervene in the federal action lawsuit filed on July 2,
  2025, captioned Perdomo, et al. V. Noem, et al. In the United States District
  Court for the Central District of California. He read as follows:

  “I am reporting out of Closed Session that the City Council unanimously
  authorized the City Attorney to take all actions needed to file a motion to
  intervene in the federal action filed on July 2, 2025 captioned Perdomo, et al. V.
  Noem, et al. in the United States District Court for the Central District of
  California.

  That case asserts that since early June 2025, federal agents have conducted
  indiscriminate immigration operations in the Los Angeles area, targeting
  individuals based on race and ethnicity without reasonable suspicion or warrants.
  The raids have reportedly led to unlawful detentions and denial of access to legal
  counsel, with detainees held in inhumane conditions.

  The defendants are various federal officials, including the Secretary of the
  Department of Homeland Security and the Acting Director of U.S. Immigration
  and Customs Enforcement, among others. They are accused of implementing
  policies that violate constitutional and statutory rights.”

  City Manager Alvarez reported pulling Agenda Item No. 4.A from the 5:30 special
  City Council meeting off the Agenda and requested the addition of the Fire
  Department under Staff Communications as Agenda Item No. 6.D.

5.  Public Communications:

  - Hassel Chinos requested a Citywide policy to identify federal agents acting
  upon the authority of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

  - Esther Perez spoke about her and fellow neighbors’ fear of leaving their homes
  and wished for a safe and secure community to live in.

  - Juan Carlos Ramirez conveyed his concerns regarding the recent actions from
  the United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement and urged assistance
  from the Police Department.
   73-205
  July 2, 2025
  - Veronica Ciafone, school administrator at East Los Angeles provided words of
  admiration to the City Council’s support to the community.

  - Alex Airusberg expressed his opinion about the recent events initiated by ICE
  and shared his appreciation to the City Council for showing support to the
  immigrants in their community.

  - Mimi Li acknowledged the City Council for their involvement in the lawsuit
  against the Trump Administration and suggested providing immigration
  resources to the community.

  - Sandy Hernandez communicated her fears about the recent actions enacted by
  ICE and requested the Police Department’s commitment to protect the
  residents of the community.

  - Hortencia Armendariz detailed her opinion about ICE and her how it is instilling
  fear in her community. She praised the support showed by the City Council for
  the immigrant community in Monterey Park and urged support from the Police
  Department.

  - Assistant Deputy City Clerk Cho received and filed a written communication
  from Dolores Seidman. She conveyed her dismay of the proposed trash rate
  change and claimed it will negatively affect the disabled and elderly.

  - Assistant Deputy City Clerk Cho received and filed a written communication
  from Bryan Ha. Bryan spoke about the recent actions displayed by ICE and
  questioned how the City Council will protect the immigrant community.

  - Police Chief Wiese provided an update on the Police Department’s
  observations during the past weeks. He announced his and the Police
  Department’s commitment to support the immigrant community.

6.  Staff Communications:

  6.A. Library: Library Manager Vera shared a PowerPoint presentation introducing
  the summer reading program to encourage children to read and win prizes. She
  highlighted previous programming from the month of June, detailed new
  programming for kids, teens and adults for the month of July, announced the
  registration date for Literacy for All of Monterey Park classes and presented a
  fundraiser to support the Friends of the Monterey Park Bruggemeyer Library at
  Panda Express on July 25, 2025.
   73-206
  July 2, 2025
  6.B. Recreation and Community Services: Recreation and Community Services
  Director Aguirre spoke about the previous events that were held in the month of
  June which include the Pride Month Festival and Independence Day Celebration.
  He detailed the proposed resolution to recognize the month of July as “Parks
  Make Life Better Month” and expressed his appreciation to the dedicated staff in
  the department.

  Recreation and Community Services Program Coordinator Esparza shared
  upcoming events which include Summer Movies in the Park; Summer Lunches
  for the Youth; Open Play Basketball for the summer; Dive in Movie Night and
  summer aquatic programing. She announced the addition of tickets to the
  Monterey Park event at the Dodger Stadium and thanked those who purchased
  tickets to the sold-out Cyndi Lauper concert at the Hollywood Bowl.

  6.C. Public Works: Public Works Director Igoe introduced the dates for the
  Monthly Compost Giveaway for the rest of the year at Garvey Ranch Park.

  6.D. Fire Department: Fire Battalion Chief Weddle informed the public about
  fireworks safety during Independence Day, announced different locations to
  purchase safe and sane fireworks and presented the Community Preparedness
  Clinic where residents can receive information on what to do during an
  emergency.

7.  Presentation

7.A.  Development Projects Update

  Economic Development Manager Torres along with Planning Manager Chow
  provided a PowerPoint presentation detailing the City’s development process and
  elaborated on projects currently in development which include the renovation of
  601 W. Garvey, improvements on 1800 W Garvey Ave, the renovation of Elite
  Restaurant, the introduction of Tumbling Dumpling, updates on 3700 Ramona
  Blvd, 1977 Saturn St, 808 W. Garvey Ave, Deerfield Plaza, 507 N Chandler Ave,
  816-824 Hellman Ave, 1969 S. Atlantic Blvd, the Celadon Mixed-Use Project,
  188 S Chandler Ave, A-1 self-storage, 283 E Garvey Ave, 100-120 N Garfield
  Ave, 126 N New Ave and introduced the new businesses that have opened at
  Atlantic Square and Atlantic Times Square.

7.B.  Economic Development Strategic Plan Update

  Economic Development Manager Torres, along with Planning Manager Chow,
  shared a presentation with an update of the Economic Strategic Plan (EDSP). He
  detailed the nine focus areas, and the three strategic focus tiers created to
  address aspects of economic growth and community well-being.

8.  Old Business: None.
   73-207
  July 2, 2025
9.  Consent Calendar Items Nos. 9.A.- 9.F.
  All items under the Consent Calendar are considered by the City Council to be
  routine and will be enacted by one motion. Specific items may be removed from
  the Consent Calendar at the request of any member of the City Council for
  separate consideration.

  Action Taken: The City Council approved and adopted Agenda Item Nos. 9.A.,
  9.B., 9.C., 9.D. and 9.E. except for Agenda Item No. 9.F. which was pulled for
  discussion, separate motion, reading resolutions and ordinances by the title only
  and waiving further reading thereof.

  Motion: Moved by Council Member Wong and seconded by Council Member
  Sanchez, motion carried by the following vote:

  Ayes:  Council Members:  Wong, Sanchez, Lo, Yang, Ngo
  Noes:  Council Members:  None
  Absent:  Council Members:  None
  Abstain:  Council Members:  None
  Recusal:  Council Members:  None

9.A.  Monthly Investment Report

  As of May 31, 2025, invested funds for the City of Monterey Park total
  $97,864,526.80

  Action Taken: The City Council received and filed the monthly investment
  report, on Consent Calendar.

9.B.  Resolution approving the Memorandum of Understanding between the City
  and the Monterey Park Police Officers' Association for the term of July 1,
  2025 to June 20, 2028

  The City of Monterey Park representatives ("City") and MPPOA representatives
  met and conferred in good faith to negotiate the terms and conditions of a new
  MOU. The parties reached an agreement to be approved by the City Council for
  a term effective July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2028.

  Discussion: The City Clerk’s office provided the public and City Council with a
  copy of the Memorandum of Understanding between The City of Monterey Park,
  California and the Monterey Park Police Officers’ Association on July 1, 2025.

  Action Taken: The City Council adopted Resolution No. 2025-R59 approving a
  Memorandum of Understanding ("MOU") between the City of Monterey Park and
  the Monterey Park Police Officers' Association ("MPPOA"). The MPPOA
  represents the police corporals and police officers in the Monterey Park Police
  Department, on Consent Calendar.
   73-208
  July 2, 2025
  Resolution No. 2025-R59
  A resolution approving the Memorandum of Understanding for contract year
  2025-2028 between the City of Monterey Park and the Monterey Park Police
  Officers’ Association

9.C.  Receive and File Housing Element Correspondence with California
  Department of Housing and Community Development

  The City Council continues to take actions to implement the City’s certified
  Housing Element and the Land Use Element (Measure JJ). Most recently, the
  City Council adopted ordinances adding an overlay zone to portions of the City
  and ensuring consistency between the General Plan/Land Use Element and the
  zoning code to continue meeting the deadlines in the Housing Element. An
  inquiry from the Department of Housing and Community Development (“HCD”)
  regarding the City Council’s actions and changes to the Housing Element's site
  inventory lists prompted the attached exchange with HCD. No action is required.
  The item is for informational purposes only.

  Action Taken: The City Council received and filed the report, on Consent
  Calendar.

9.D.  Maintenance Agreement with Trojan Technologies Corp.

  The Water Division is requesting approval of an Agreement with Trojan
  Technologies Corp . (“Trojan”) for preventative maintenance services of the
  advanced-oxidation ultraviolet treatment system at the Delta Plant. The term is
  for one year at a cost not to exceed $315,000.

  CEQA (California Environmental Quality Act):
  These actions are exempt from additional review under the California
  Environmental Quality Act (California Public Resources Code §§ 2100, et seq.,
  “CEQA”) and CEQA Guidelines (14 California Code of Regulations §§ 15000, et
  seq.) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines § 15061(b)(3), the common sense exemption
  that CEQA applies only to projects which have the potential for causing a
  significant effect on the environment applies to the recommended action. It can
  be seen with certainty that there is no possibility that the proposed action has a
  significant effect on the environment.

  Action Taken: The City Council authorized the City Manager to execute an
  Agreement with Trojan Technologies Corp., (“Trojan”) in a form approved by the
  City Attorney, for the maintenance of its Advanced-Oxidation Ultraviolet
  Treatment System at a cost not to exceed $315,000, on Consent Calendar.
   73-209
  July 2, 2025
9.E.  A Resolution Declaring the Month of July as “Parks Make Life Better”
  Month in the City of Monterey Park

  During July, the Recreation and Community Services Department celebrates
  "Parks Make Life Better” month. By designating July as "Parks Make Life Better"
  month, the City of Monterey Park, Recreation and Community Services
  Department urges all residents to enjoy and recognize the social, physical,
  mental, economic, environmental, and community benefits of our parks. As we
  observe "Parks Make Life Better" month, we recognize the vital contributions of
  our employees and volunteers, who all contribute to making parks and recreation
  facilities a great place to visit. These dedicated staff members and volunteers
  keep our parks clean and safe for visitors, and they coordinate and organize
  special events, youth programs, swim lessons, educational classes, senior
  activities, and health and fitness programs. They ensure that parks and
  recreation facilities are safe and accessible places to enjoy.

  Action Taken: The City Council adopted Resolution No. 2025-R60 declaring the
  month of July as “Parks Make Life Better” Month in the City of Monterey Park, on
  Consent Calendar.

  Resolution No. 2025-R60
  A resolution of the City Council of the City of Monterey Park declaring the month
  of July 2025 as Parks Make Life Better Month

9.F.  Consideration to provide Letter of Support for SB 627, the "No Secret
  Police Act," and SB 805, the “No Vigilantes Act," on behalf of the City

  SB 627 would require law enforcement officers at all levels—local, state, and
  federal—to show their faces and be identifiable via uniforms when interacting
  with the public, with certain exceptions such as for SWAT teams and medical-
  grade masks.

  SB 805 would extend crimes regarding impersonating a peace officer, firefighter,
  or public employee, to include willfully and credibly impersonating any of those
  entities through any means for the purpose of defrauding another.

  SB 805 would require personnel of a law enforcement agency operating in
  California to visibly display identification that includes either a name or badge
  number to the public when performing their duties. The bill would exempt
  personnel operating undercover from these provisions. The bill would make a
  violation of these provisions a misdemeanor. The bill would define personnel of a
  law enforcement agency as any officer of a local, state, or federal law
  enforcement agency or any person acting on behalf of a local, state, or federal
  law enforcement agency.
   73-210
  July 2, 2025
The bill would also authorize law enforcement to request an alleged government
employee to present identification when there is probable cause or reasonable
suspicion of a crime including, without limitation, impersonating a peace officer,
firefighter, employee of a public utility or government agency, or member of a
search and rescue team, or when there is a legitimate safety concern.

Existing law, the Bail Fugitive Recovery Persons Act, regulates bail fugitive
recovery agents, defined as a person given written authorization by the bail or
depositor of bail and contracted to investigate, surveil, locate, and arrest a bail
fugitive and any person employed to assist the bail or depositor of bail to
investigate, surveil, locate, and arrest a bail fugitive. This bill would prohibit a
person authorized to apprehend a bail fugitive from using that position for the
purposes of immigration enforcement and would require a person authorized to
apprehend a bail fugitive to keep a defendant’s immigration status confidential,
as specified.

The combination of SB 627 and SB 805 would increase transparency by law
enforcement personnel when contacting the public.

Public Speakers:

- Yun Wang spoke about the recent actions enacted by ICE and conveyed his
  opinions about the Police Department. He spoke about the recent statements
  provided by Representatives Judy Chu and Norma Torres regarding this issue.

- Juanita Medina depicted the fear felt by her and her daughter regarding the
  current events led by ICE.

- Teresa Real provided a written Urgency Ordinance for consideration as
  documentation. She detailed the proposed Ordinance as an opportunity to
  protect the residents from the actions enacted by ICE. She spoke with approval
  of Agenda Item No. 9.F. and requested the City Council to amend the letter to
  state the need to make SB 627 and SB 805 urgent law.

- Bryan Ha provided his opinion about the actions implemented by ICE and
  questioned the steps the city will take to help protect the citizens.

- Hortencia Armendariz conveyed her approval of Agenda Item No. 9.F. and
  commented on the City’s need to have a signed commitment solidifying their

Action Taken: The City Council sent a letter of support for California Senate Bills
627, the "No Secret Police Act," and 805, the “No Vigilantes Act,” on behalf of the
City, as amended to draft a letter to the federal immigration authorities to urge
them to respect the constitutional rights of individuals and to prioritize immigration

   73-211
  July 2, 2025

  Sanchez, motion carried by the following vote:

10.  Public Hearing

10.A. Adoption of an Ordinance Amending Title 6 of the Monterey Park Municipal
  Code in its entirety regarding public health services and incorporation of
  Title 11 of the Los Angeles County Code

  The City of Monterey Park contracts with the County of Los Angeles Public
  Health Department for public health services. In order for the Los Angeles
  County Department of Public Health to continue to perform public health
  services, the City needs to amend Title 6 of the Monterey Park Municipal Code
  and adopt Title 11 of the Los Angeles County Code regarding health and safety.
  At the May 21, 2025, City Council meeting, the Council approved the City
  Manager to enter into an agreement with the Department of Public Health,
  approved the introduction and waived the first reading of the ordinance. The
  public hearing was set for June 18, 2025. The City complied with regulatory
  notice requirements by posting notice of the public hearing on June 5, 2025, and
  June 12, 2025, in the Monterey Park Progress newspaper. Second reading and
  adoption of this Ordinance is recommended. If adopted, the ordinance will take
  effect in 30 days.

  Action Taken: The City Council opened the continued public hearing at 9:46
  p.m. to take testimonial and documentary evidence; with no registered speakers,
  closed the public hearing at 9:46 p.m. and after considering the evidence,
  adopted Ordinance No. 2264 amending Title 6 of the Monterey Park Municipal
  Code.

  Motion: Moved by Council Member Wong and seconded by Council Member Lo,
  motion carried by the following vote:

  Ayes:  Council Members:  Wong, Sanchez, Lo, Yang, Ngo
  Noes:  Council Members:  None
  Absent:  Council Members:  None
  Abstain:  Council Members:  None
  Recusal:  Council Members:  None
   73-212
  July 2, 2025
  Ordinance No. 2264
  An Ordinance amending and restating Monterey Park Municipal Code Chapter
  6.04 in its entirety to incorporate Title 11 of the Los Angeles County Code
  regarding Health and Safety regulations within the City’s jurisdiction

10.B. Adoption of an Ordinance Updating the Fire Hazard Severity Zones
  ("FHSZ") Pursuant to Government Code section 51178

  The Office of the State Fire Marshal ("OFSM") finalized the adoption of the State
  Responsibility Area Fire Hazard Severity Zone ("FHSZ") map, which became
  effective April 1, 2024. The State Fire Marshal is mandated by Government Code
  section 51178 to identify levels of fire hazard based on consistent statewide
  criteria and the expected severity of fire hazards. Government Code section
  51179 requires the State Fire Marshal to make recommendations of fire hazard
  severity zones to local agencies, including the City, for their designation and
  adoption by ordinance. The finalized map shows that the City of Monterey Park
  does not include any areas within the FHSZ identified by the State Fire Marshal.
  At the June 4, 2025, City Council meeting, the Council approved the introduction
  and waived the first reading of the ordinance. The public hearing was set for
  June 18, 2025. The City complied with regulatory notice requirements by posting
  a notice of the public hearing on June 12, 2025, in the Monterey Park Progress
  newspaper.

  CEQA (California Environmental Quality Act):
  The City reviewed the environmental impacts of the extension under the
  California Environmental QualityAct (Public Resources Code §§ 21000, et seq.
  "CEQA") and the regulations promulgated thereunder (14 Cal. Code of Regs. §§
  15000, et. seq., the "CEQA Guidelines"). This activity contemplates
  administrative actions and will not result in any direct or indirect physical change
  in the environment. Accordingly, no further review is required.

  Discussion: Interim Fire Chief Haberle shared a PowerPoint presentation
  depicting the proposed Fire Hazard Severity Zone map.

  Action Taken: The City Council opened the continued public hearing at 9:47
  p.m. to take testimonial and documentary evidence; with no registered speakers,
  closed the public hearing at 9:47 p.m. and after considering the evidence,
  adopted Ordinance No. 2265 adopting the finalized State Responsibility Area
  Fire Hazard Severity Zone map.
   73-213
  July 2, 2025
  Motion: Moved by Council Member Sanchez and seconded by Mayor Pro Tem
  Yang, motion carried by the following vote:

  Ayes:  Council Members:  Wong, Sanchez, Lo, Yang, Ngo
  Noes:  Council Members:  None
  Absent:  Council Members:  None
  Abstain:  Council Members:  None
  Recusal:  Council Members:  None

  Ordinance No. 2265
  An Ordinance adopting the state Fire Marshal Fire Hazard Severity Zone map by
